images.caption: American Planes Bomb Jap Positions In The Solomons. A cloud of smoke and charred bamboo trees mark what was once a Japanese fuel and ammunition dump on Kolombangara Island in the New Georgia group of the Solomon Islands in the South Pacific. U.S. air and naval forces made two successive attacks on the position.

images.caption: 80-G-700018:  USS St. Louis (CL 49) whose bow was blown by a Japanese torpedo at the Battle of Kolombangara, 12/13 July 1943.   St. Louis received a temporary bow at an advanced base in the Pacific.  With this bow, the cruiser was able to return to a west-coast navy yard for more permanent repairs.  Photograph released:  July 24, 1945.  U.S. Navy photograph, now in the collections of the National Archives.  (2017/02/14).
